title: Compute conductor claimableLanes from ownership disjointness, not lane grouping alone
why: archkit_conductor emitted three lanes as concurrently claimable, but pr-based-landing (lane-lane-reconcile-stage) owns src/lib/goals.mjs — the same file all three goals in lane-frontmatter-colon-escaping own. Dispatching the emitted plan verbatim would have put two parallel worktree workers on the same file and guaranteed a clobber. The conductor already computes the file-overlap conflict set; claimableLanes should be filtered by it rather than leaving the human to catch it.
exitCriteria: claimableLanes excludes any lane whose frontier CGRs have owned-path overlap with another lane already in the claimable set, so the emitted set is safe to dispatch verbatim in parallel

The excluded lane is still surfaced (e.g. a deferredLanes or blockedByOverlap slice) with the overlapping paths and the lane it collides with, so the conductor knows why it was held and when it frees up
Per-CGR granularity is preserved: a lane is not withheld wholesale when only some of its frontier CGRs overlap — the non-overlapping ones stay claimable
The coarse tests/ path does not by itself withhold a lane, since nearly every CGR declares it; overlap detection distinguishes a shared directory from a shared file
A test asserts that two lanes owning the same src file are never both emitted as claimable in one pass
contextExcerpt: Lane-integration dispatch pass, 2026-08-02. The conductor's own conflicts[] array already listed {finalize-project-inheritance, pr-based-landing} and {payload-goal-path, pr-based-landing} on src/lib/goals.mjs with crossLane:true, yet both lanes were still emitted as claimable in the same pass.
